details:
Project Details – AstroQuest

Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer for Moon and Mars Missions

AstroQuest is an educational space exploration project designed to introduce young learners to the scientific, technological, and engineering challenges of human missions to the Moon and Mars. Its central idea is to transform complex space exploration concepts into an engaging and interactive learning experience, allowing students to explore the responsibilities and challenges faced by astronauts when planning and sustaining missions beyond Earth.

The project combines mobile application development, 3D visualization, and space science research to create an interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer. Developed using Flutter and Dart, the application provides a dedicated learning environment with an interactive interface and 3D viewing capabilities. Blender supports the development of 3D models and visual assets, while the project's simulation engine contributes to its mission-training concept.

AstroQuest focuses on the interconnected challenges of establishing and maintaining a sustainable human outpost in extraterrestrial environments. Learners are introduced to essential mission requirements, including life-support systems, radiation protection, power management, food production, communication, resource allocation, and scientific activities. These elements highlight the importance of planning, prioritization, and decision-making when resources are limited and environmental conditions are challenging.

Rather than presenting space science as a collection of facts, AstroQuest aims to make learning more experiential through mission-oriented exploration and interactive visual experiences. It encourages young learners to think about how different systems depend on one another, why astronauts must make difficult decisions, and how those decisions can influence mission safety and success. By connecting scientific knowledge with practical mission challenges, the project seeks to strengthen curiosity, critical thinking, problem-solving abilities, and interest in STEM education.

The scientific research and development of AstroQuest are informed by publicly available NASA resources, including the NASA DONKI database, the Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), and information related to the Artemis program and Mars exploration. These resources provide valuable context for understanding space weather, the effects of the space environment, and the challenges associated with future human exploration missions.

The project is developed and maintained through GitHub, which supports source-code management, version control, and collaborative development. The complete project repository, including its available application code, documentation, and supporting resources, can be explored here:

Project Repository:
https://github.com/purnorabby/AstroQuest

A supplementary project demonstration video is also available to provide a visual overview of AstroQuest, its concept, and its development:

Project Demonstration Video:
https://youtu.be/aRULjb3WDAw

AI tools were used in a supporting capacity during selected stages of development, including brainstorming, research assistance, writing, and coding support or troubleshooting. These tools served as supplementary resources; the project's concept, development direction, implementation, and overall work remain the responsibility of the team.

Our Vision

Our vision is to make the challenges of human space exploration more accessible and understandable to the next generation. Through AstroQuest, we hope to inspire young minds to look beyond Earth, explore scientific possibilities, and develop the knowledge and skills needed to become tomorrow's scientists, engineers, innovators, and space explorers.
